title: Beyond Moore: Co-Optimizing AI from Systems to Materials - Semiwiki
gist: At the OCP APAC Summit, Applied Materials' Subi Kengeri argued conventional node scaling alone cannot sustain AI compute growth; leadership will hinge on co-optimizing materials, devices, packaging, cooling and power delivery as one system, with energy-efficient performance and heterogeneous integration as the new frontiers.

themes.theme: AI inflection and the scaling limit

insights.claim: Conventional semiconductor node scaling alone cannot sustain the required improvement in AI compute; the next era is constrained by energy, interconnects, packaging complexity and the speed of turning materials innovation into manufacturable systems.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Value migrates from lithography scaling toward packaging, materials and system co-optimization plays.

insights.claim: AI demand is accelerating the semiconductor industry toward one trillion dollars in annual revenue.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Confirms secular TAM expansion underpinning the sector.

insights.claim: Across recent accelerator generations, performance cost fell roughly threefold while AI-server power consumption also rose about threefold, making energy-efficient performance the decisive metric.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Power and cooling opex over a system's life now dominate economics, favoring energy-efficiency IP.

insights.claim: The keynote set a target of a 10,000-fold improvement in energy-efficient performance by 2040, requiring simultaneous innovation across logic, memory and system integration.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Frames a multi-decade roadmap requiring cross-domain innovation, not just transistor shrink.
insights.quote: The keynote set an ambitious target: a 10,000-fold improvement in energy-efficient performance by 2040.

insights.claim: Capital expense is paid once while electricity and cooling costs continue throughout a system's life, shifting the optimization boundary toward operating efficiency.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Reframes datacenter TCO around lifetime power rather than upfront capex.

insights.claim: Gate-all-around transistors can deliver roughly 30% lower power and 15% higher performance, while backside power distribution can add about 30% density and 10% performance.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Quantifies the incremental gains from next-node device architectures.

insights.claim: Advanced packaging is projected to deliver up to 1,000 times higher I/O density and ten times lower energy per bit, with hybrid bonding scaling from 10,000 toward one million I/Os per square millimetre below 0.05 picojoules per bit.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Packaging interconnect becomes the primary lever for bandwidth and energy per bit.

insights.claim: Package complexity is exploding: a 2000s server processor had one die and a complexity factor of one, a contemporary AI GPU integrates 118 dies reaching a factor near 32,000, and future system-in-package designs may exceed 400 dies and a factor of 600,000.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Complexity growth is the new scaling axis, favoring advanced packaging, assembly and test suppliers.

insights.claim: Assembly and packaging can represent more than half of process cost, and assembly, packaging and test together can exceed 80% of process cost.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Value is migrating from front-end lithography to back-end assembly, packaging and test.

themes.theme: STCO and EDA as the enabler

insights.claim: Complexity at this scale cannot be solved by sequential device, package and system optimization; System Technology Co-optimization uses EDA to concurrently solve thermal, mechanical, signal-integrity and power effects.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Expands the addressable market for multiphysics, co-optimization EDA tooling.

insights.claim: For hyperscalers cost per transistor gives way to cost per useful function, so package architecture, cooling, power-delivery losses, repairability and workload placement must be evaluated together.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Changes buyer decision criteria toward system-level cost of useful compute.
insights.quote: Cost per transistor gives way to cost per useful function.

insights.claim: Open interfaces are essential so chiplets from multiple suppliers can be qualified, combined and upgraded; Applied Materials positioned its STCO platform, reusable chiplet prototype vehicle, UCIe and OCP participation and EPIC center as collaboration mechanisms.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Chiplet interoperability standards are becoming a competitive battleground.
